$comment: design §7.2 (the four closed vocabularies), §7.3 (proposal content and the structural rules), §7.4 (placement, through tables/placement_rules.json and packets/placement_contract.md), §7.5 (the ranking keys this carries), §10.4 (ledger-only dispositions carry no operations); plan WP-12. This schema holds the SHAPE of one S7 answer. What it may not hold is the contract: the allowed (kind, diagnosis) -> disposition pairs, the structural rules and the placement rules live in tables/allowed_pairs.json, tables/structural_rules.json and tables/placement_rules.json, read by runlib/placement.py, because a vocabulary written twice is two authorities. So `disposition` is an enum here and WHICH disposition is allowed for this candidate is not. `unknowns` is where a named state of the derivation (a unit outcome not derived, delivery not assembled, an arc confirmation undetermined) is carried forward instead of being read as a negative answer.
title: S7 proposal

keep_record_named.$comment: The active keep record a reduce or merge supersedes; structural rule KEEP_GUARDED reads it.

harmful.$comment: A reduce of a unit that is covered and followed is allowed only when the unit is harmful (§7.2's condition `reduce_when_harmful`, read by runlib/placement.py). The flag is the model's claim, and the reason field says on what.

requires_R.$comment: A core item needs an R comparison; §10.4 and WP-20 read it, and an item admitted by adjudication in the second pass is awaiting_R and enters no F this run.

before_state_sha256.$comment: Every operation carries the expected before-state hash of its target (§7.3); `absent` is the create case, where the target does not exist yet and the hash of nothing would be a hash of something.

unit_states.$comment: Set by code, never by the model (runlib/stage_propose.py with_before_states): for a merge, the state of each unit that lives in another file than the target, as S7 read it. S11 holds that file to it before it removes the unit; a merge whose other-file unit carries no state is refused.

names.$comment: For a route: the path the entry points at. runlib/sequencing.py reads it to ask whether an intermediate tree would hold a route to nothing.

korean.$comment: null only where the item is not user-facing; the reason belongs in reasons.proposal.

layer.$comment: Judged against tables/placement_rules.json `destinations.order`, not enumerated here: one authority for the layers.

carrier.$comment: null for a disposition that carries no operations; a placed item names the file or entry that carries it. The pattern refuses a control character only - a single line. WHICH layers exist and whether the path is relative are `runlib/placement.destination_problems`'s, so one rule has one authority; the pattern is here because a schema can say 'one line' without restating anything.

reasons.$comment: The person reads these, so they are Korean; the share is a non-blocking diagnostic of S9b, never a gate here.

unknown.$comment: A named state of the derivation this proposal would have rested on, carried forward by name: the field, the state as the derivation spelled it, and what the proposal does about it.

counter_or_null.$comment: Nullable: null where no counter can resolve the observation.

gate_change_or_null.$comment: Nullable: null where the item is not author-side.

expected_observation_or_null.$comment: Nullable: null where the disposition asks for no observation. The policy of runlib/validate.py admits a nullable as a type list and refuses oneOf, so the shape is stated once and this twin carries the null.

consumer.$comment: Who the instruction is aimed at. tables/placement_rules.json `consumers.reads` says what each consumer reads; a consumer it does not name is not refused here, because the table is the authority on the set.

artifact_form.$comment: `instruction` when the item instructs someone; something else when it is code, a gate or a hook registration.

blocking.$comment: Whether the proposed gate or hook BLOCKS. Required by the rules' scopes when the destination is gates or hooks.

criterion.$comment: `semantic` when a person must judge it, `decidable` when code can. A blocking gate on a semantic criterion is refused.

judges.$comment: Whether the proposed hook JUDGES. A hook that blocks or judges is outside a hook's charter.

situation_promoted_items.$comment: How many promoted items already share this situation. §7.4 asks for at least five before a new guide.

situation_covered_by_guide.$comment: Whether a guide already covers the situation.

names_situation_of_guide.$comment: For a C principle placed in a guide: whether it names the situation of the guide that holds it.

owner_only.$comment: For session-level injection: whether the item is the owner's alone.

placement_claims.$comment: The claims §7.4's decidable rules read. Every field is present and may be null, and `placement.py` refuses a null for a rule whose scope the proposal is in (PLACEMENT_INPUT_ABSENT) - so a null is an honest 'not applicable here' and never a way past a rule. `typology` is NOT here: it is the candidate's own type, which S6 derived, and an answer that carried it would give that field two sources.
